short: A test that buries a specific fact deep inside a huge block of text to see if a model can still find it.
definition: A needle-in-a-haystack test checks how well a model actually uses a long context window, rather than just accepting one. A short fact (the "needle") is inserted at a chosen position inside a much longer, unrelated document (the "haystack"), and the model is asked a question that can only be answered by finding it. Running this at many needle positions and context lengths reveals whether a model reads evenly across a long input or quietly loses track of information in the middle or at awkward spots, even while claiming to support a huge context window.
